claim: EC2 declarative policies centrally enforce configurations for Amazon EC2, Amazon VPC and Amazon EBS across the organization; their attributes include VPC Block Public Access, Image Block Public Access, Allowed Images Settings, Instance Metadata defaults, Serial Console Access and Snapshot Block Public Access.
question: Which service settings can an EC2 declarative policy enforce?

values.display: Amazon EC2, Amazon VPC, and Amazon EBS
VPC Block Public Access and Image Block Public Access
Allowed Images Settings, Instance Metadata defaults, Serial Console Access

qualifiers.scope: EC2 declarative policies in AWS Organizations

evidence.quote: EC2 policies allow you to centrally declare and enforce desired configurations for Amazon EC2, Amazon VPC, and Amazon EBS at scale across an organization.
In Figure 1, there is a generated account status report, which shows uniformity across accounts for the following attributes: VPC Block Public Access and Image Block Public Access.

The generated account status report shows inconsistent accounts for the following attributes: Allowed Images Settings, Instance Metadata defaults, Serial Console Access, and Snapshot Block Public Access.

claim: The Snapshot Block Public Access attribute of an EC2 declarative policy controls whether Amazon EBS snapshots are publicly accessible.
question: How can an organization stop every account from making EBS snapshots public?

values.display: Controls if Amazon EBS snapshots are publicly accessible

evidence.quote: Policy effect: Controls if Amazon EBS snapshots are publicly accessible.

The generated account status report shows inconsistent accounts for the following attributes: Allowed Images Settings, Instance Metadata defaults, Serial Console Access, and Snapshot Block Public Access.

claim: Most drift can be resolved by administrators, but some must be resolved at once: deleting the Security OU or required Control Tower roles makes the console ask you to reset the landing zone, and moving shared accounts out of the foundational OU is remediated by updating the landing zone.
question: How is drift resolved in Control Tower?

values.display: Most types of drift can be resolved by administrators
instructing you to reset the landing zone immediately
you must update the landing zone

evidence.quote: Most types of drift can be resolved by administrators. A few types of drift must be resolved immediately, including deletion of an organizational unit that the AWS Control Tower landing zone requires.
If you delete it, you'll see an error message instructing you to reset the landing zone immediately.
To remediate this type of drift, you must update the landing zone.

claim: Control Tower uses CloudFormation StackSets by default to set up resources in your accounts, deploying one stack set instance per account and Region.
question: How does Control Tower deploy its baseline resources into accounts?

values.display: uses CloudFormation StackSets to set up resources
one stack set instance per account and Region

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower uses CloudFormation StackSets to set up resources in your accounts, by default.
AWS Control Tower deploys one stack set instance per account and Region.

claim: With Organizations you can create accounts programmatically and centrally provision recommended resources and permissions to them with AWS CloudFormation StackSets, for example per group of development and production accounts.
question: How can you provision baseline resources into many accounts without Control Tower?

evidence.quote: You can simplify account creation by programmatically creating new accounts using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), SDKs, or APIs, and centrally provision recommended resources and permissions to those accounts with AWS CloudFormation StackSets.
Create separate groups to categorize development and production accounts and use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to provision services and permissions to each group.

claim: With auto-enrollment on, moving an account into a registered OU enrolls it with that OU's baseline and controls, for existing and newly created accounts; moving it to an unregistered OU or the root unenrolls it and Control Tower removes the baseline resources and controls.
question: How do accounts enter and leave Control Tower governance with auto-enrollment?

values.display: The account automatically receives baseline resources and controls
Move the account to an OU that is not registered
removes all deployed baseline resources and controls automatically

qualifiers.condition: auto-enrollment enabled; landing zone 3.1 or later

evidence.quote: The account automatically receives baseline resources and controls from that OU. This applies to both existing accounts and newly created accounts (which are created in the organization root by default).

To unenroll an account: Move the account to an OU that is not registered with AWS Control Tower, or to the root of the organization. AWS Control Tower removes all deployed baseline resources and controls automatically.
